minutes.headline: Sewer board debates charging an extra connection fee when a home is split into more units
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Sewer Commission reviewed ongoing manhole and pump station repair work, approved end-of-year billing adjustments after a leak-driven $6,000 outlier bill, and discussed delinquency rates on sewer bills. The bulk of substantive discussion concerned whether the town should charge an additional connection fee when a single-family home is converted into multiple dwelling units, with no bylaw change made but the director directed to draft language for the next meeting; commissioners also voted to keep their current roles unchanged.

what_happened.line: The commission debated charging an extra sewer connection fee when a single-family home is split into more dwelling units, but made no bylaw change and directed the director to draft language for the next meeting.
Commissioners voted 5-0 to accept end-of-year billing adjustments, including a large one-time bill tied to a prolonged water leak that skewed the quarter's totals.
A specific property's betterment and connection charges were discussed as the test case for whether added living space should trigger a further connection fee.
The manhole rehabilitation contract is finished except for one manhole near Prospect Street/Laurel Lane, where unsafe gas readings mean a new bid is needed to replace it.
Commissioners voted 5-0 to keep all commission roles (chair, vice chair, clerk) unchanged.

why_it_matters: Any new connection fee for homes converted into additional dwelling units would raise costs for property owners doing that kind of renovation, once bylaw language is drafted and brought back.
The sewer operations and maintenance contract is being rebid ahead of its August expiration, which touches how sewer service is delivered without interruption.
Sewer bill delinquency and late-fee levels affect the health of the sewer enterprise fund that all ratepayers depend on.
